thread:
maria: Heads-up — today during a burst test eu-west-1 gpu-dense nodepool hit IP exhaustion and a bunch of pods failed to bind. Not a full outage but enough to surface risk.
karim: Ugh. Is this the new `gpu-spot-dense` pool with /26 subnets per AZ?
sam: Yeah, the pool is using small secondary IP ranges (we followed the default from the TF module). Pods ~= 60 per node via CNI + gpu-metrics containers, blew past ENI allocation quickly.
jess: Note: cluster-autoscaler does scale up but the cloud provider returns no capacity because subnets are full. CA logs show `no available IPs` for nodes it tried to create.
maria: Summary: autoscaler + tiny subnets + spot fallback = pods Pending even though we have GPU capacity elsewhere. Need a terraform/helm automation plan so this doesn't recur.
karim: Proposal: 3-prong approach — 1) Terraform: make nodepool module create dedicated larger secondary CIDR per pool (eg /22), tagged for GPU pools. 2) Helm: cluster-autoscaler values tuned to prefer balanced nodegroups and tolerate scale up delays. 3) Infra: pre-warm small on-demand buffer and a DaemonSet to pre-pull heavy images.
sam: Agree. Also add an early failure metric: `PodUnschedulable: reason=InsufficientIPs` alarm in prometheus -> ops-runner.
ops-runner: +1, will add an alert. Suggest threshold: >5 pods pending for 2m with reason=InsufficientIPs.
jess: For the Helm bit, here's a minimal values snippet I tested locally that reduced oscillation: 
```yaml
autoscaler:
  enabled: true
  extraArgs:
    balance-similar-node-groups: true
    expander: least-waste
    scan-interval: 10s
    scale-down-unneeded-time: 10m
    max-empty-bulk-delete: 4
  podAnnotations:
    cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: 'false'
```
karim: Terraform snippet for the nodepool module (simplified):
```hcl
module "gpu_nodepool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/modules//nodepool"
  name   = "gpu-spot-dense-eu"
  instance_type = "p4d"
  min_size = 0
  max_size = 20
  subnet_secondary_cidr = "10.50.0.0/22" # bigger CIDR for IP headroom
  labels = { workload = "gpu-inference", pool = "dense" }
  taints = [{ key = "gpu", value = "true", effect = "NoSchedule" }]
}
```
maria: Important: ensure the TF module also sets an explicit tag that the nodepool belongs to CA nodegroups list (we've seen ambiguity break scale-to-zero).
sam: Also add automation to reconcile subnet sizes: if usage > 80% for 24h, open a PR to increase CIDR or create new pool. Could be a small lambda + terraform plan job.
jess: On image startup latency: we should add a small on-demand buffer pool (1-2 nodes per AZ) with `node.kubernetes.io/instance-type=...` and `taint: gpu:NoSchedule` removable for canary workloads. Pre-pull daemonset example:
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: image-prepull-gpu
spec:
  selector: { matchLabels: { name: "image-prepull-gpu" } }
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: { name: "image-prepull-gpu" }
    spec:
      tolerations:
        - key: "gpu"
          operator: "Exists"
          effect: "NoSchedule"
      containers:
        - name: prepull
          image: busybox
          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "docker pull <heavy-image> || true; sleep 3600"]
          resources: { requests: { cpu: "10m", memory: "32Mi" } }
```
karim: Ops question: for spot pools, should the autoscaler prefer on-demand fallback by default when it sees IP exhaustion? Or should we proactively resize subnets?
maria: Prefer subnet resize + on-demand buffer. On-demand fallback is fine short-term but costy. If IPs are the limiter, fallback doesn't help because same subnet limits.
ops-runner: I'll add an autoscaling runbook step: if InsufficientIPs and CA logs show `not enough IPs in subnet`, then escalate to infra with the `subnet-resize` playbook.
sam: Can we automate a canary TF apply that increases one AZ's secondary CIDR then drains test nodes to validate? Would need infra approvals.
jess: We can build a pipeline job: `infra/canary-subnet-resize` that runs TF plan/app against a single AZ and creates a `terraform-apply` PR. Add a safeguard: require manual approval if plan adds > /22.
karim: Ops metrics to watch during rollout: PodPending count for reason Unschedulable, CA scale-up latency, new node creation failures, ENI allocation errors from cloud provider, cloud API rate limits.
maria: Timeline:
- karim + jess: PR for TF module changes (bigger secondary CIDR + tagging) — by EOD tomorrow
- sam: Helm values PR for CA + test in staging — today
- ops-runner: alert + runbook update — end of day
- deploy-bot: schedule a canary test next Wed in eu-west-1 (low traffic window)
deploy-bot: scheduled: infra/canary-subnet-resize — Wed 03:00 UTC, will run dry-run first and DM approvers.
maria: Thanks all. Keep replies here if you hit blockers. :thumbsup:
karim: I'll start the TF branch and ping for reviews.
sam: I'll smoke test CA config in staging and post results.
jess: Will add the prepull daemonset as a kustomize overlay and link the PR.
ops-runner: Added alert and runbook entry.
maria: Closing the loop — once canary passes we'll roll to other AZs with terraform automation.
